en: Aerosol cans explode if heated because the gas inside expands and increases pressure.
Mixing bleach and vinegar creates toxic chlorine gas, so these cleaning liquids must never be combined.
Metals conduct heat quickly, which is why cooking pots have plastic or wooden handles to prevent burns.
Water expands when it freezes into ice, so leaving a full sealed glass bottle in the freezer will shatter it.
Stirring sugar into warm water dissolves it faster than in cold water, helping you quickly prepare oral rehydration drinks.
Oil and water do not mix, which is why we use soap to break down grease on our hands.
Chewing food thoroughly is a physical change that breaks it into smaller pieces, helping your stomach digest it easily.
Rubber and plastic are electrical insulators, which is why wires are coated in them to prevent electric shocks.
Rust is a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and water, weakening metal structures like bicycle frames.
Evaporation turns liquid sweat into a gas on your skin, absorbing heat and cooling your body down.
Drinking seawater is dangerous because its high salt concentration draws water out of your cells, causing severe dehydration.
Filtering dirty water through clean cloth and sand removes solid particles, making it safer to boil and drink.
